name: Phentermine
route_note: oral tablet or capsule once daily in the morning, labelled for short-term use (a few weeks) in the US

discovery.note: A substituted phenethylamine structurally related to amphetamine, developed as an appetite suppressant in the 1950s.

tagline: The most prescribed US weight-loss drug, an amphetamine relative that curbs appetite
summary: Phentermine is a sympathomimetic amine that suppresses appetite and is used short-term for obesity together with diet and exercise. It is the most widely prescribed anti-obesity medicine in the United States, is a controlled substance because of its relationship to amphetamine, and is combined with topiramate in Qsymia.
mechanism: Phentermine is taken up into nerve terminals and causes release of noradrenaline (and to a lesser extent dopamine and serotonin) from presynaptic stores, partly via TAAR1 agonism and reversal of monoamine transporters.

Increased noradrenergic signalling in the hypothalamus reduces appetite and may increase energy expenditure. Peripheral sympathetic effects raise heart rate and blood pressure, which limit its use in cardiovascular disease.
uses: Short-term adjunct for exogenous obesity (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with risk factors)
Chronic weight management in combination with topiramate (Qsymia)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Phentermine is approved in the US as an appetite suppressant.

history.title: Controlled substance
history.detail: Phentermine is placed in Schedule IV of the US Controlled Substances Act.

history.title: Fen-phen
history.detail: A study by Weintraub popularises the combination of fenfluramine and phentermine ('fen-phen').

history.title: Fenfluramine withdrawn
history.detail: Fenfluramine and dexfenfluramine are withdrawn after reports of valvular heart disease; phentermine remains available.

history.title: Qsymia
history.detail: FDA approves phentermine/topiramate extended-release (Qsymia) for chronic weight management.

history.title: Lomaira
history.detail: A low-dose 8 mg tablet (Lomaira) is approved, allowing dosing up to three times daily.

serious: valvular heart disease (reported, mainly with fenfluramine combination)

facts: In 'fen-phen' it was fenfluramine, not phentermine, that was withdrawn for heart valve damage in 1997.
Phentermine is a Schedule IV controlled substance in the US.
